title: BACKGROUND OVERVIEW
texts: BACKGROUND OVERVIEW
Recall: the Problem and the Gap
RECALL
HIADs when deployed: the inflated toroidal stack that replaces a rigid TPS on the vehicle.
Source: CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures/HIADsDeployed.png, thesis Chapter I.
• THE ACTUAL PROBLEM: a rigid shield cannot outgrow the fairing, so entry mass is capped, and above 50 km the continuum CFD that sized it stops being valid.
• WHY IT BITES: an inflatable packs small and inflates large, but its surface deforms under load, and that deformation changes the flow field and the heat transfer.
• THE RESEARCH GAP: no framework couples parametric geometry, DSMC in the transitional regime and GA optimisation; HIAD work stays on RANS/LES and manual sweeps.
• THE TRADE: area buys drag and thins the flux per unit area, yet peak heating, heat load, ballistic coefficient and mass move together, so the envelope is optimised, not chosen.
Four sentences, each compressed from Chapter I: Background, Problem Statement and Research Gap.

title: OBJECTIVE AND RESEARCH SCOPE
texts: OBJECTIVE AND RESEARCH SCOPE
Recall: the Objective and the Scope
RECALL
The HIAD as an overview: the inflatable aeroshell against the rigid body it replaces, as the thesis draws it.
Source: Hiad_DesignSpec.png from CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures, the vehicle specification drawing of Chapter III.
• THE OBJECTIVE: build and validate one framework that predicts a HIAD aerothermal load and optimises its geometry for survivability, using SPARTA DSMC and a genetic algorithm.
• THE SCOPE: rigid, fully inflated 6-toroid HIAD; 5-species air with VSS collisions; 0.01 < Kn < 1 at 50 to 60 km; 2D axisymmetric or 3D; GA on an analytic cost.
• WHAT RIGID MEANS: the fully inflated shape is frozen for the run: no pressure-load deflection, no fabric wrinkling, no ablation or recession, and no fluid-structure coupling.
• HOW IT IS CHECKED: Sutton-Graves and SPARTA surface quantities against IRVE-3 flight data, a four-level grid independence study, and a fixed seed 42 for re-runs.
Out of scope: packing and deployment mechanics, toroid structural sizing and the PINN path; the FTPS itself is flexible, only its shape is frozen.

title: LITERATURE: THE GAP AND THE NOVELTY
texts: LITERATURE: THE GAP AND THE NOVELTY
Literature: The Gap
RECALL

Gap one:
HIAD aerothermal work is mostly continuum CFD, invalid above 50 km where Kn exceeds 0.01

Gap two:
design studies are manual parametric sweeps, with no geometry generation coupled to DSMC

Gap three:
survivability is not optimised jointly on heat load, peak flux, ballistic coefficient and mass

Novelty:
one pipeline coupling CadQuery geometry, SPARTA DSMC and a genetic algorithm on an analytic cost
The gap the thesis claims, stated before the method. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE SOLVER
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE SOLVER
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
The equation the particle solver answers, and the cross-section it scatters with.
The Boltzmann equation governs the distribution function of the gas
Streaming and the force term balance the collision term
DSMC answers it statistically instead of solving it directly
The variable soft sphere cross-section sets how the particles scatter
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: kinetic theory, a dilute gas with binary collisions and molecular chaos; the VSS law closes the cross-section.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE SIMULATION SETUP
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE SIMULATION SETUP
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
The SPARTA grid of the reference run at grid factor 0.7, and the solver chain that feeds it.

One uniform Cartesian grid:
139 by 139 cells at grid factor 0.7, 19,321 cells in all.
The grid is finer than the local mean free path in the shock layer.
Body of revolution with a toroidal stack; five design variables.
Geometry and flight point feed SPARTA and the Ada/SPARK solver.
Source: CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures/grid_mesh_map_smooth.png, thesis figure archive, the computational grid figure of chapter 04.
How the simulation is set up. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE MESH
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE MESH
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
The relation that decides how small a cell of the grid may be.
Knudsen number is the mean free path divided by the length L
The mean free path is one over square root two, pi, d squared and n
The cell width must stay below the mean free path of the gas
That is why the reference grid is finer than the local spacing
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: continuum validity is set by the Knudsen number, so a cell must be finer than the local mean free path.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE GRID INDEPENDENCE
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE GRID INDEPENDENCE
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL

Four refinement levels of the same geometry and flight condition: peak heat flux left, drag right.
Both series fall faster as the grid refines, so neither can be extrapolated to a converged value.

Levels:
five, 70x70, 100x100, 139x139, 200x200 and 250x250 Cartesian cells on one geometry and condition

Peak flux:
2.059, 1.946, 1.797, 1.536 and 1.580 MW per square metre

Flux steps:
minus 5.49, minus 7.66, minus 14.53 and plus 2.85 percent, reversing at the finest level

Drag:
48.012, 45.918, 45.697, 44.064 and 44.107 kN, steps of minus 4.36, minus 0.48, minus 3.57 and plus 0.10 percent

Verdict:
non-monotone, so no Richardson limit and no converged value; the two percent test fails at every pair and the peak flux carries a roughly fifteen percent grid band
Source: CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures/grid_independence_qoi.png, the thesis five-level grid study of chapter 4, reused unchanged.
The mesh quality and the grid independence. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE CONVERGENCE
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE CONVERGENCE
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
Why sampling uncertainty survives grid refinement in this project.
Statistical noise falls with the square root of the samples
The peak surface ID migrates with refinement, so the sampled maximum moves between cells
The two percent grid test fails at every adjacent pair in the recorded study
Particles per cell fell from 62.4 at L4 to 34.1 at L5, so part of the spread is sampling
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: the central limit theorem, so the Monte Carlo error falls as one over the square root of the sample count.

texts: METHODOLOGY: THE SOLVER CONVERGENCE

Normalised residuals of the three monitored quantities against particle-time step.

Residual:

Monitored:
drag coefficient, lift coefficient and the per-element heat flux average

Fall:
about three orders of magnitude between step 100 and step 2200

Scatter:

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE CONVECTION
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE CONVECTION
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
The correlation that carries the convective load of every candidate.

Scaling:
the flux grows with the cube of the velocity

Radius:
it falls with the square root of the nose radius

Constant:
1.7415 times ten to the minus four, fitted for air

Reduction:
a small Knudsen number turns Boltzmann into Navier-Stokes; its stagnation layer gives this shape

Empirical:
a fit to the Fay-Riddell layer, Sutton and Graves, NASA TR R-376, 1971
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: similarity of the stagnation-point boundary layer in a hypersonic stream.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE CONVECTION CHANNEL
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE CONVECTION CHANNEL
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
The Sutton-Graves correlation that carries the convective load of every candidate geometry.
q = C_SG sqrt(rho/R_N) V^3 with C_SG = 1.7415e-4 for Earth air.
At 3378 m/s and a 1.5 m nose radius it gives 15.36 W/cm^2.
The particle solver ranks geometries; it gives no absolute flux.
At the candidate nose radius the screening flux is 25.36 W/cm^2.
Source: sutton_graves_parametric.png from CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures, the correlation figure of chapter 03.
The first of the three heat-flux channels. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE CONDUCTION
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE CONDUCTION
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
The balance that splits the arriving heat between the stack and the surface.
The wall balance is conduction across the stack plus re-radiation
Radiation enters as eps sigma T^4, so the grey-body term grows with the fourth power
R is the sum of the ply resistances, 0.3056 m^2 K per watt
The backface model raises the temperature with its thermal lag
The chain runs one dimension along the stack, element by element
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: conservation of energy in one dimension, with a lumped backface and constant ply properties.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE CONDUCTION CHANNEL
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE CONDUCTION CHANNEL
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
Through-thickness and per-ply temperature of the FTPS layup at the final step of the reference run.
Heat enters the hot face and conducts through the five-ply layup.
Stack resistance 0.3056 m^2K/W over 3,648 surface elements.
Back face stays at 300 K while the hot face reaches 1327.2 K.

Lateral:
each element also exchanges heat with its neighbours, through a lumped conductance
Source: CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures/tps_ply_conduction.png, thesis figure archive, the ply conduction figure of chapter 04.
The second of the three heat-flux channels. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE LATERAL COUPLING
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE LATERAL COUPLING
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL

The in-plane term that closes the thermal chain after the one-dimensional solve.
It is lumped, not a second PDE: one conductance between an element and its neighbours.

Model:
a lumped conductance between an element and its neighbours, applied after the one-dimensional solve

Magnitude:
0.0083 W per square metre on the reference run, against a 143,760 convective load

Ratio:
about 6e-8 of the load, so the in-plane exchange never decides survivability

Verdict:
negligible for this geometry, so the stack keeps its one-dimensional solve
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
The lateral coupling term. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE RADIATION
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE RADIATION
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
The equilibrium that sets the temperature of the hot face of the vehicle.
A grey body radiates q = eps sigma T to the fourth power
The emissivity of the outer Nicalon SiC ply is 0.75
Equilibrium divides the incoming flux by eps sigma and takes the root
The surface temperature is therefore set by the radiation alone
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: Stefan-Boltzmann radiation from a grey, diffuse, opaque surface in view of space, in steady balance.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE RE-RADIATION CHANNEL
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE RE-RADIATION CHANNEL
Methodology: DSMC CFD
RECALL
Temperature through the five-ply stack, hot face to back face, of the reference run.
The hot face radiates as a grey body, q = eps sigma T^4, eps 0.75.
A convective load of 143,760 W/m^2 arrives at the surface.
Reradiation takes 140,399 W/m^2, conduction only 3,362 W/m^2.
So the surface temperature is set by the radiative balance.
Source: CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures/tps_ply_stack_temperature.png, with the overlapping footnote band of the thesis figure cropped in this folder.
The third of the three heat-flux channels. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE DESIGN SPACE
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE DESIGN SPACE
Methodology: Optimization Pipeline
RECALL
The design vector and the relations that turn it into the geometry of the vehicle.

The design vector holds five variables:
X1, X2, X3, Nt and the mass
X1 is the body radius, X2 the torus radius and X3 the half-cone angle
The nose radius follows the body radius through the ratio kappa, 0.3667

The box holds the 6-toroid Rapisarda baseline:

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE COST FUNCTION
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE COST FUNCTION
Methodology: Optimization Pipeline
RECALL
The composite cost of the genetic algorithm: four weighted terms, a penalty and the heat load.
The cost is a weighted sum of four dimensionless terms

Heat load:
W_HL times Q over Q_target is the first and heaviest objective
Stagnation flux enters through q over q_ref
The ballistic coefficient is squared against its reference, drag one sided
A penalty term pushes the design back inside the limits of the box
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: weighted-sum scalarisation of four dimensionless objectives, evaluated at one fixed exposure time.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE COST FUNCTION
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE COST FUNCTION
Methodology: Optimization Pipeline
RECALL
The recorded convergence of the composite cost of the genetic algorithm over 38 generations.

The cost is analytic:
evaluating it needs no solver call

Four dimensionless terms:
heat load, stagnation flux, ballistic coefficient, drag
All terms are non-negative, so the cost is at least zero by construction
The weight on the drag term selects the regime of the heat-load and drag trade
Source: ga_convergence.png from CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures, drawn by figures/make_ga_figures.py from the recorded campaign.
How a design is scored. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE GENETIC ALGORITHM
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE GENETIC ALGORITHM
Methodology: Optimization Pipeline
RECALL
The operators and the stopping rule that govern the recorded campaign.
A population of 50 designs runs for at most 200 generations

Tournament:
three designs drawn at random, the cheapest one wins

So k_t sets the selection pressure:
3 is mild, a larger k is harsher
Crossover is applied with 0.7, each gene mutates with probability 0.1
It stops when the best cost stops improving by 1e-6 over 20 generations
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: a bounded, closed-form objective, so the search needs no solver call and can afford fifty by two hundred.

title: METHODOLOGY: THE GENETIC ALGORITHM
texts: METHODOLOGY: THE GENETIC ALGORITHM
Methodology: Optimization Pipeline
RECALL
The path of the generation-best design through the design box, coloured by generation.
Population of 50 designs evolved for at most 200 generations
Tournament selection k = 3, BLX-alpha crossover 0.7, alpha 0.5, Gaussian mutation 0.1
Elitism copies the best two unchanged, so the best cost never rises
The campaign stopped on stagnation after 38 generations, 1900 evaluations
Source: ga_design_trajectory.png from CurrentThesisFinalReport/figures, drawn by figures/make_ga_figures.py from the recorded campaign.
How the population evolves. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE DOUBLE PASS
texts: GOVERNING EQUATION: THE DOUBLE PASS
Methodology: Optimization Pipeline
RECALL
The correction factor of the second pass and the corrected cost it produces.
Pass 1 searches in closed form and re-simulates only its own winner
The factor c is the solver flux over the Sutton-Graves flux of that run
It is clamped between 0.5 and 2.0 so one bad run cannot invert the cost
Pass 2 re-runs the same algorithm with the heat load weighted by c
Source: typeset from chapter 3 of the thesis by tools/make_equation_pictures.py.
Fundamental: the fidelity ratio is taken within one run, and only the thermal term of the cost carries that bias.

title: PREVIOUS ISSUE 3: THE FOURTH POWER IS THE RADIATIVE SINK
texts: PREVIOUS ISSUE 3: THE FOURTH POWER IS THE RADIATIVE SINK
Issues: Issue 3
RECALL

What the frame actually solves:
Not Fourier alone, but the wall balance (T - T_back)/R + eps*sigma*(T^4 - T_inf^4) - q_w + G*T - S = 0, with the in-plane term G*T - S from the lateral coupling.

Where the fourth power comes from:
The surface sheds heat by re-radiating, q_rad = eps*sigma*T^4. Conduction carries the flux through the stack; radiation fixes the temperature at which that flux leaves, so T^4 is the boundary condition of the conduction problem, not a conduction law.

Why it forces an iteration:
Fourier is linear, the sink quartic, so no linear solve closes the balance. The slope 1/R + 4*eps*sigma*T^3 + G stays positive, so the root is unique and bisection finds it.

At the design point:
143,760 in = 140,399 re-radiated + 3,362 conducted W/m2, a ratio of 41.8 to 1. eps = 0.75 puts the wall at 1,348 K, where the sink moves 417 W/m2 per kelvin, 12.4 % of the conducted flux.
Why the conduction frame carries a fourth power. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.

title: WHY T^4 SITS OUTSIDE FOURIER
texts: WHY T^4 SITS OUTSIDE FOURIER
Issues: Issue 3, where the fourth power comes from
RECALL

Where the fourth power is born:
Planck's spectral exitance integrated over every frequency gives q = sigma*T^4; the fourth power is the moment of x^3/(e^x - 1), pi^4/15, with zeta(4) = pi^4/90. It is an integral, not a fitted exponent.

Why it is not a second conduction term:
Fourier carries heat into the stack; Stefan-Boltzmann carries it out to space. At one wall node these are two parallel sinks sharing one T, each counted once: (T - T_back)/R + eps*sigma*(T^4 - T_inf^4) = q_w. Folding sigma*T^4 into k would spend the same photons twice.

When radiation joins the conduction term:
the flux diffuses as q_rad = -k_R grad T, with k_R = 16*sigma*T^3/(3*kappa_R), a volumetric conductivity rather than a wall flux. It holds only in an optically thick medium; the shock layer here is not, so the term is dropped.

What the solve then faces:
f(T) = (T - T_back)/R + eps*sigma*(T^4 - T_inf^4) - q_w + G*T - S. The slope 1/R + 4*eps*sigma*T^3 + G is positive, so the root is unique; that 4*eps*sigma*T^3 is the tangent of the same quartic, 417 W/m2 per kelvin at 1,348 K, not a new term.
One radiative term at the wall, one conductive term through the stack, two parallel paths at one node.

title: PREVIOUS ISSUE 4: WHAT EACH GENETIC PARAMETER DOES
texts: PREVIOUS ISSUE 4: WHAT EACH GENETIC PARAMETER DOES
Issues: Issue 4
RECALL

Population 50, at most 200 generations:
Fifty is ten times the five design variables and a quarter of the 200-individual cap. The campaign stopped on stagnation at generation 38, so it spent 50 x 38 = 1,900 evaluations, the budget the DSMC campaign had.

Tournament k = 3, two elites:
The best of three random draws wins, so the best design is picked with probability 1 - (1 - 1/50)^k: 2 % at k = 1, 5.9 % at k = 3, 63.6 % at k = 50. Enough pressure to climb, mild enough to keep diversity. Two elites are copied untouched.

Crossover 0.7, BLX-alpha 0.5:
Seven pairs in ten are blended and three in ten copy the parents through. The blend samples the interval widened by alpha = 0.5 of the parental gap, so a child can step outside its parents without leaving the design box.

Mutation 0.1, sigma 0.1 of range:
Each of the five genes mutates with probability 0.1, so half a gene per child on average, displaced by N(0, sigma) with sigma = 0.1 of that gene's range and clamped to its bounds. The run stops when the best cost has not improved by 1e-6 for 20 generations.
Why each value and what it does; seed 42 keeps the campaign reproducible. The narration stays editable in PowerPoint.
